To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) spectral and spatial convolution and transposed convolutions can be used to learn representative features of HSIs and improve HSI classification performance and (b) GAN based models with fully connected CRF constraints can achieve superior HSI classification performance using limited amounts of annotated HSI data.

spectral and spatial convolutional layers can be integrated into the fundamental components of deep learning models for HSI classification, and that GAN CRFs can effectively enhance the generalization ability of deep learning based HSI classification models.

spectral and spatial convolutional neural networks and generative adversarial neural networks with fully connected conditional random fields can be effectively used for supervised HSI and semi supervised HSI classification, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
supervised and semi supervised HSI classification.

the design of deep learning models that can effectively learn discriminative features from HSIs and improve the classification performance of these models by incorporating the characteristics of HSI data.
supervised HSI classification using deep learning, semi supervised HSI classification, and semi supervised HSI segmentation using probabilistic graph models.

this thesis presents a novel framework for supervised and semi supervised HSI classification by exploiting the characteristics of HSI data.

spectral spatial deep neural networks and GANs can improve HSI classification performance by taking the data attributes and the inherent properties of HSIs into consideration.
